title.narrative: ROAS / IRAQ / Modernising Urban Knowledge (MULK): Transitioning to E-land Governance in Iraq Programme

description.narrative:
Impact: Improved housing, land, and property (HLP) rights for the benefit of all Iraqis, including displaced populations and those in the most vulnerable situations.
Outcome 1: Improved legal, institutional and operational framework regulating e-land governance and Housing, Land & Property Rights Digitisation.
As part of Iraq’s long-term development agenda and reform process, through the project titled “Modernising Urban Land Knowledge (MULK)” the Government of Iraq (GOI) with support from the United Nations Human Settlements Programme (UN-Habitat) seeks to reform and modernise its land governance and management framework by supporting the creation of a land record digitisation system and in developing the technical specifications and implementation plans for digitised e-land administration and e-cadastre systems. The project aims to initiate the necessary processes for improving security of tenure and land governance systems through initiating legislative and regulatory reforms, developing the framework for streamlining and making transparent land-related administrative processes, and by promoting access to data that can influence investment and land use decisions. Modernising land governance systems is essential to Iraq's reform agenda and is crucial for advancing equality and facilitating future investment, paving the way for a more productive and prosperous economic future for all Iraqi citizens.
The proposed project aims to support the Government of Iraq in reforming and revising the HLP legal and regulatory framework, and in modernising land governance through software development to digitise land records, and to develop technical specifications and implementation plans for e-land registry and e-cadastre systems which includes enhanced technological capacity on the ground. The project will create the legal framework for ICT-based solutions and establish sound implementation plans for digitising property records, automating the property registration systems, developing electronic issuance of title deeds and transfers, and in building a modern cadastre system.
Digitising property records as is proposed in the scope of this project will ensure that there are secure back-up files that prevent fraudulent land claims and reduce opportunities for corruption. Building a framework for the future development of a comprehensive digital land-registry will support the GOI in determining the necessary steps and resources required to undertake the endeavour. By deploying a user-friendly land registration system, the GOI will be able to streamline and make more efficient land administrative processes and procedures. Likewise, by building the technical framework and implementation plan for the development of a robust e-cadastre, the GOI will be supported in doing the necessary preparatory work in pursuing this enormous undertaking. In the long run and with sufficient commitment and investment, the GOI can build stronger land management systems which will also support addressing climate change through facilitating evidence-based urban planning, enabling greater opportunities for sustainable development patterns.
Throughout the project, UN-Habitat will support the GOI through policy dialogue and direct technical assistance, capacity development, and mentorship activities. The project aims to create more equitable and inclusive HLP rights and land governance systems that prevents land-based conflicts, displacement, increases access to HLP ownership documentation, improves security of tenure and other HLP ownership rights-related issues, and enhances e-land governance through necessary reforms and by setting in motion a digitised property database and e-land administration framework. Through engaging in policy dialogue with the EU, CSO’s, state institutions and government actors the project supports Iraq’s reform agenda as the country transitions from a humanitarian response to a long-term development agenda. The project also supports this transformation through delivering capacity-building, technical trainings, and awareness raising activities are fundamental to the project’s success. Specifically, government staff can leverage the technical specifications set forth under this project to create new ICT-based solutions to maximise land administration e-governance capacity. The project takes on a continuum approach starting with building the framework for the digitisation of land records and building a digital database of land records in pilot locations- establishing the technical framework and plan for a land administration framework - and then further progressing to building the necessary plan and specifications for a robust e-cadastre system.
